verdict: Nu grew revenue 53% to $5.0B and profit 56% to $871M in IFRS terms, passing 135 million customers as its Mexico business reached break-even.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue $5.0B vs $3.2B in Q1 2025, in dollars (IFRS accounting basis)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Diluted earnings per share, vs $0.11 a year ago

kpis.label: Customers
kpis.note: 135.2 million total, up from 118.6 million a year ago; about 4 million added in the quarter

kpis.label: Deposits
kpis.note: Customer deposits held with Nu, up 22% year over year; credit portfolio $37.2B, up 40%

segments.name: Interest income & instrument gains
segments.note: Interest earned on loans, credit cards and investments, plus gains on financial instruments — the core money a bank makes from lending. Reported as 'Interest income and gains on financial instruments'.

segments.name: Fee and commission income
segments.note: Fees and commissions from cards and other services customers use in the app.

opex.name: Customer support and operations
opex.note: Customer support and day-to-day operations for an app-only bank with no branches.

opex.name: General and administrative expenses
opex.note: Staff, technology and running the company — the biggest operating cost block.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Other operating expenses as reported in the statement.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped 56% in dollars
takeaways.text: Net income reached $871M, up from $557M a year ago in dollar terms, with return on equity of 29%. On Nu's managerial view, revenue passed $5 billion for the first time ($5,315.5M).

takeaways.title: Still adding millions of customers
takeaways.text: Nu added about 4 million customers to reach 135.2 million — over 115 million in Brazil, 15 million in Mexico and approaching 5 million in Colombia. Mexico reached break-even in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Loan-loss costs spiked seasonally
takeaways.text: Credit loss allowances closed at $1.79B, up 33% in the quarter on seasonality, portfolio growth and mix. Expected credit losses of $1,718M were the biggest single cost after funding, and the 15–90 day delinquency ratio rose to 5.0% on the usual first-quarter pattern.

otherDetail: Other income of $20M, less a $1M share of losses from associates — net +$19M.
footerNote: Nu is a digital bank; cost of revenue is mostly interest paid to depositors and loan-loss provisions. Figures are the IFRS accounting P&L.
